prompt: Write part of a deposition transcript (about 400 words) of a plaintiff in a car accident lawsuit. The defense lawyer asks (lines start with 'Q:') and the plaintiff answers (lines start with 'A:'). Accident: side impact at intersection in Sugar Land, Texas. Injury: concussion. Ask about the accident, treatment and daily life. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1320; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather not give my full name on the record for this part. You can use the name that's on the case caption.

Q: That's fine. Where were you on the day of the collision?

A: I was driving north on a surface street in Sugar Land, Texas, heading toward a shopping center. It was mid-morning and the sky was clear.

Q: Walk me through the intersection. Did you have a traffic signal?

A: Yes, there was a signal. My light was green when I entered the intersection. I remember that clearly because I had just accelerated through it.

Q: What happened next?

A: A vehicle coming from my right ran the red light and struck the driver's side of my car. The impact was on the side, right where my door is. My head hit the window frame, and then everything went blurry.

Q: Did you lose consciousness?

A: I don't think I was fully unconscious, but I was dazed. I couldn't tell you how long it was before I could think clearly again. People were talking to me and I was answering them, but I didn't feel like myself.

Q: Who did you speak with at the scene?

A: A responding officer and a paramedic. They checked my eyes and asked me questions. I got a headache almost right away, and it got worse over the next few hours.

Q: After the scene, what treatment did you receive?

A: I was taken to an emergency room and they diagnosed a concussion. I was told to rest in a dark room for several days and to avoid screens as much as possible. I went to a follow-up with my primary care doctor and then started seeing a neurologist.

Q: Have you had any ongoing symptoms?

A: Yes. Headaches still come a few times a week. Bright lights bother me, and I get tired by mid-afternoon. I have trouble concentrating on longer tasks at work, and I've had to re-read emails more than once.

Q: How has this affected your daily life?

A: I used to coach my kid's soccer team on weekends and I've had to step back from that. I also stopped driving at night for a while because the glare made me dizzy. My spouse handles more of the errands now, and I feel frustrated about that.

Q: Are you currently receiving any treatment?

A: I'm doing vision therapy and some cognitive exercises twice a week. My neurologist says recovery can take time, and I'm following her recommendations.
